title: Contract-era compatibility guardrails and feature-flag migration plan
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Goal: establish a practical, enforceable semantic versioning and deprecation policy for the serving runtime that enables predictable upgrades for customers and safe evolution for engineers. This ticket proposes: 1) a concrete semantic versioning flavor (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH + channel tags), 2) a breaking-change classification matrix with explicit rules for when MAJOR bumps are required vs. when deprecation headers and migration shims suffice, 3) LTS channel guarantees and allowed backport windows, 4) rollout gate automation (canaries, progressive % ramps, rollback triggers), and 5) a minimal upgrade tooling surface (rt-upgrade CLI + CI compatibility checks + changelog conventions) to reduce manual migration work.
acceptance_criteria: Semver rules documented and merged to runtime README + Confluence (includes examples)
CI: semver-lint and compatibility-check job runs on runtime PRs and blocks merges for detected class-A breaking changes without a documented mitigation plan
Deprecation header implemented: servers emit X-Redwood-Deprecation with target removal version and date
LTS policy page published: defines supported patch window, minor acceptance rules, and backport SLAs
Rollout automation blueprint added to ops repo and demo canary pipeline configured (1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%) with health/latency/error rollback triggers
rt-upgrade CLI MVP (scan + migration suggestions) available in internal tools and documented
Golden prompt compatibility suite added and runs as part of nightly CI with alerting on regressions
timeline: 2025-01-20: Engineering review complete; added classification matrix
2025-01-28: Confluence policy published (draft), security review scheduled
2025-02-02: CI semver-lint prototype merged; canary pipeline PR opened

2025-03-10: Target production rollout of deprecation header and rollout automation
release_action_plan: Publish policy and versioning examples to public docs and customer-facing changelog
Notify top-10 customers two release cycles before MAJOR changes; provide migration guides and migration assistance (SE time budget)
Enable deprecation headers by default for new runtime builds; allow opt-out via feature-flag for internal testing
Run canary with 1% traffic for 24h, expand to 10% for 6h, then 50% for 12h, then 100% if metrics stable
Monitor: p50/p95 latency, error-rate by route, token cost delta, top-10 customer request traces; automatic rollback on >3x error-rate or >2x p95 increase
